Stocks' shock absorber could be masking a much uglier downside.

Peter Tchir says popular income funds may be propping up stocks, but outflows could trigger a rapid downturn

"One problem I think the stock market has that Bitcoin doesn't have is all the vol suppression strategies tied to it."

"Everywhere you look, there's income oriented funds that are selling vol in the S&P 500, selling it on Nasdaq 100, selling it on individual stocks."

"I suspect it's part of why the buy the dip has been so successful. I would watch, like, the JEPIs and JEPQs of the world to see if they get any outflows."

"I suspect, though, if it breaks, it gets really ugly very quickly. And you would get a very rapid downturn as those sorts of strategies unwind."

"All these vol suppression strategies are much bigger and much more prevalent than they were 5, 10 years ago."

text:
Verizon's CEO said today that SpaceX will need at least 4-6 years and $300B-$500B to fully build out its @Starlink Mobile U.S. carrier network:

"Their service just can't compete with a terrestrial network. In suburban and urban areas, where 98% of our revenues are, we're somewhere between 100x–1,000x more efficient than they are. We know exactly what they're going to do. We know who they're talking to on towers. There's no magic wand. There's no secret sauce. There's no shortcut.

They're going to look at 65,000–80,000 macro sites. They're going to need backhaul, RAN, and a tremendous amount of spectrum. It's going to take a minimum of four to six years to fully build that out. It's going to cost hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars, I assume somewhere between $300 billion and $500 billion.

zh_summary: （由 @TheStalwart 轉發）@aRishisays 解釋巴西選舉衝擊為何顯得非比尋常：在政治保持中間路線延續時，重要選舉很少見；爆冷通常發生在60對40而非80對20的格局；這是二元、非反身性事件，與聯儲局會議不同。
en_summary: (Reposted by @TheStalwart) @aRishisays explains why the Brazil election shock felt extraordinary: vital elections are rare when politics has centrist continuity, and upsets usually come from 60/40 setups, not 80/20; it is a binary, non reflexive event unlike the FOMC.
text:
Two reasons:

1. Elections that are this vital have usually been rare (getting more frequent now - think France, US, Canada last year, Brazil today). Most of the time elections don’t matter much for markets when there is some kind of centrist continuity to politics. 

2. When they do matter, upsets happen but typically from a 60-40, 66-33 setup instead of 80-20. 

Combined, this Brazil election becomes a huge surprise and hence feels extraordinary. But then again, it’s a binary, non-reflexive event (unlike the FOMC) so the odds don’t really have predictive power. It’s just a collective guess, and so expected to miss every now and then.

text:
The numbers in Anthropic’s S-1 are hard to ignore. $ANT

The S-1 went public this morning. Everything below is quoted straight from it.

On demand vs supply:
“we have historically operated in a compute-constrained environment in which demand for compute has exceeded the supply available to us.”

On $TSM:
“we have not always been able to obtain sufficient quantities of chips on a timely basis.”

On memory, HBM is “largely manufactured by SK hynix Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., and Micron Technology, Inc.” $SKHY $MU 

On data center equipment:
Power, cooling, generators and networking gear “must be ordered years in advance” and “require substantial pre-delivery payments that we may not recover if our plans change.”

Then look at the disclosed compute agreements:

> $AVGO ~$161.2B in five-year leases for TPU capacity
> $GOOGL at least $114.5B through 2033
> $AMZN at least $110.0B through 2036
> $MSFT at least $44.9B through 2033
> $NVDA GPUs through SpaceXAI (up to $120.5B), Nscale (~$44.6B) and Lambda (~$41.3B)
> $AMD Helios racks, over $20B if fully procured

Revenue grew 1,368% YoY in Q2. Compute and infrastructure expense grew 300%. Net revenue retention is ~900%.

The Fed is expected to hold rates steady Wednesday, but it is a closer call on the data than the market-implied probabilities suggest.

The case for hiking: 
1) The hot September CPI and PPI underscore a second straight lost year for getting inflation down
2) With a Dec hike widely expected, hawks will argue that there's less to gain from waiting six weeks given the cost of falling further behind
3) Hawks will also argue that policy isn't restrictive and needs to be

1) If officials still think this is a 2-3 hike recalibration, spacing out remaining moves costs little. "Being six weeks late is a manageable risk," says Rob Kaplan
2) Back-to-back moves could signal a faster cycle than officials intend
3) After several officials signaled no rush, and Warsh’s silence let odds of a hold build, a surprise hike days before the midterms would be a jolt. The Fed has raised rates right before elections, but not as a surprise

SpaceX has officially announced that they have secured $40 billion in the largest GPU financing ever.

The company entered into a $40B master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing ever.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen:
"SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we're seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers."

Transaction Details:
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

He asks traders how they identify each regime and how much risk each deserves.
text:
6 PLAYBOOKS FOR 6 DIFFERENT MARKET REGIMES

Last week’s firm-wide @smbcapital meeting was about better adapting to different market regimes.

Which begs the question - what types of market regimes are there for discretionary traders? And what playbooks should we be running for each of them?

I’ll start and you all can expand on this in the replies.

Obviously this is far from exhaustive and kept high-level, but I think this should lead serious traders to do some deep reflection of their own. 

1. Theme-driven bullish market. Markets like this one favor momentum strategies, swing longs, overnight momentum, IPOs, and headlines relevant to the driving theme.

Early summer of 2026 certainly fell under this with AI as the driver and leading sectors like DRAM / cloud computing.

2. Macro-driven markets. Think in the spring during the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict, think  2025 Trump tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine war. Due to the randomness and volatility of these headlines, this market highly favors breaking news trading as well as trading move-to-move, while greatly reducing overnight exposure and swing exposure. 

3. Range-bound market. Think of the last couple months, where we've had no prevailing theme and most indices have stayed range-bound while the leaders from the prior cycle corrected. text:
$META

META OFFICIALLY ENTERS THE CAPITAL RAISING GAME THROUGH SELLING MORE OF THEIR STOCK.

Meta announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two equity offerings:

- $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements.

- $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock.

The company is also considering a separate $60 billion offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares, potentially beginning in Q1 2027. The nonvoting class was introduced on earnings last week and will result in a 2-for-1 stock split. 

The total raise so far will be around $95B, $10B more than Google’s $85B equity offering from a few months ago. 

$NVDA NVIDIA, $AMD, and $AVGO Broadcom have also expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing a combined $5 billion of Meta shares…which basically means the suppliers of chips to Meta will now be taking a direct equity stake into them. Meta already has warrants that convert into shares for 10% of $AMD if it holds above $600 in the future. 

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.
